title: Window clog causing priority imbalance and elevated tail-latency - action plan
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Summary: A production incident on 2026-03-09 exposed a recurrent 'window clog' pattern in the continuous batching pipeline. The clog manifested as groups of low-priority, long-sequence requests that prevented timely formation of latency-sensitive batches, producing priority inversion and 99.9th-percentile latency spikes for interactive customers. This ticket captures the investigation, immediate mitigations, and planned engineering work to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At ~2026-03-09T18:12 UTC we observed sustained tail-latency degradation on several US-hosted inference pools. Traffic shows normal qps but a sudden rise in long-sequence low-priority requests from a small customer cohort. Continuous batch windows stalled waiting for coalescence; high-priority short requests waited across multiple windows and experienced 3-6x latency on p99. No hardware failures; autoscale didn't trigger because CPU/GPU utilization remained moderate.
timeline: 2026-03-09T18:12 UTC - Alert: p99 latency > 250ms for route /v1/generate (US-east-1)
2026-03-09T18:15 UTC - Initial triage: identified long-sequence (>2k tokens) requests increasing in tail latency cohorts
2026-03-09T18:25 UTC - Mitigation 1: Applied flow-control rule to cap max inflight tokens per customer (hotfix) - immediate p99 improvement
2026-03-09T19:05 UTC - Mitigation 2: Enabled short-window preemption (experimental flag) to allow small high-priority batches to cut in
2026-03-10 - Post-incident deep dive began; collected trace spans, batching histograms, and KV eviction logs
root_cause: A combination of scheduler policy and workload skew: (1) continuous-batcher window duration adapts to inter-arrival estimates but over-inflated when a small cohort sent long sequences, causing windows to wait for coalescence; (2) priority handling deferred preemption of windows already aggregating low-priority requests, resulting in priority inversion; (3) lack of per-customer inflight token limits allowed a single tenant to monopolize KV slots and batch capacity during bursts.
immediate_mitigations: Applied per-customer inflight token soft cap (hotfix) to bound long-sequence impact
Deployed experimental preemption flag to allow short high-priority batches to form if wait > 20ms
Enabled additional tracing for batch formation latencies and per-cohort KV eviction metrics
Notified on-call and customer success teams; advised affected customers with suggested client-side rate smoothing
long_term_action_items: Implement 'window-gap' detector that breaks windows predicted to be clogged by long sequences
Add hard per-tenant token and slot quotas with graceful degradation (queue backpressure + 429 guidance)
Refactor scheduler to support soft-preemption and micro-reservation for high-priority tiny batches
Extend batching simulator with real traffic replay from the incident to test policies
Add telemetry: per-window cohort composition, wait-time histogram, and preemption events to Console dashboards
Create an automated canary for long-sequence bursts that validates fallback policies under load

notes: We intentionally avoid aggressive global throttles; objective is to localize protections to tenant-level and provide observable fallbacks. This ticket will track both code changes and Console observability to ensure SLOs recover under similar future bursts.
